counterfactual_missing_items: No malignant lymphocytes or atypical lymphoid infiltrate to support lymphoma; instead, histopathology shows microbial structures and inflammation
No documented organism or source for sepsis beyond the skin; the skin lesions and histopathology point to a specific fungal infection, not just neutropenic sepsis
decisive_items: thin-walled (5–15 μm), pauciseptate hyphae with minimal branching
thick-walled ovoid sporangia (5–20 μm) that stained strongly with PAS, GMS, and Giemsa
response.rationale: R3 is strongly supported by pathognomonic raw histopathology spans: angioinvasive microbial structures, pauciseptate hyphae, and thick-walled sporangia staining with PAS/GMS/Giemsa, in a necrotic skin lesion from an immunocompromised host. R2 explains only the fever and neutropenia but not the skin findings. R1 is contradicted by the absence of malignant cells and presence of microbial structures.

rejected.why: The raw histopathology spans show microbial structures and inflammation, not malignant lymphocytes; the skin lesions are better explained by an infectious process.
While neutropenia and fever are present, this candidate does not account for the necrotic skin lesions or the specific fungal structures seen on histopathology.
